newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-HODDLE PUTS WINNING BEFORE ENTERTAINING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HODDLE PUTS WINNING BEFORE ENTERTAINING.

text.p: England boss Glenn Hoddle said on Friday he will put winning ahead of entertaining when his side take on Poland in their World Cup qualifying match on Wednesday.
"We could send a great exhibition team out," said the former England playmaker, who followed his principles by naming a squad packed with showmen for the Wembley clash.
"But at this level we would lose the game."

Paul Gascoigne, Steve McManaman, David Beckham, Matthew Le Tissier, and Paul Merson -- five of the most exciting players in Britain -- are in Hoddle's squad, but Gascoigne is the only real certainty to start.

"When you play at club level you have a set of supporters to try to please and a principle of what you want to see," Hoddle told a news conference at training camp. "It's different to how you work in this set-up.
"To a certain degree this is all about getting it right on the night, not necessarily about keeping a set of supporters happy with how you play.
"At this level, first and foremost you have to win. Some days it might not be as attractive as you would wish it in your heart but your mind tells you that's the right thing to do."
England go into the match boosted by their last-four showing in the European championship, and Hoddle said he was optimistic about his side's World Cup chances.
"I would not have taken the job if I didn't think there were quality players in the squad," he said. "It's a hard enough job in the first place without the players to do it.
The former Chelsea boss, preparing for his first home match as England manager, hinted he might make changes to the side that beat Moldova 3-0 last month.

"I have to pick a team that's right to win any given game and that might change for different types of reasons," he said. "You have to come up with what you feel will give the opposition problems and combat what they're good at.
